scenarios.description: Container fingerprinting followed by probing of the escape surface: runtime sockets, service-account tokens, host mounts, writable kernel interfaces, capabilities, user namespaces.
scenarios.notes: Probe-only emulation of a T1611 attempt. Nothing is exploited.

scenarios.description: Credential hunting: cloud and SSH keys, tokens, .env files, recursive secret grep, other processes' environments.
scenarios.notes: All secrets in the lab image are fake.

scenarios.description: Cloud metadata probing (real link-local address and the lab mock), DNS probing, then TCP fan-out across the lab subnet looking for container APIs.
scenarios.notes: Lab network is internal; no traffic leaves it.

scenarios.description: Dense run of ~28 sensitive-path probes, mostly failing, then one success used immediately. Agent-speed.
scenarios.notes: Same actions as recon-burst-human; only the pace differs.

scenarios.description: Same probes as recon-burst-machine at human pace (1-3 s between steps).
scenarios.notes: tempo-burst must NOT fire here; content-based rules still should.

scenarios.description: Complete chain: fingerprint, escape probe, credential access, metadata, network fan-out, exfiltration to the lab collector.
scenarios.notes: Exfiltrated archive contains only fake data and goes to the lab collector.

scenarios.description: Python dev loop: venv, offline pip install, pytest, edit, pytest, compileall.
Node dev loop: offline npm ci, run, npm test.
Everyday git: init, commits, branch, merge, log, diff.
Build step: compileall, checksum all files, tarball, unpack and verify.
Environment check that overlaps with fingerprinting: cgroup limits, OS info, ~/.ssh presence, env.
Legitimate coding-agent session at machine speed: broad reads, greps, config lookups that fail, edit, venv + tests, commit.
